subject: Pre-sales: peak curve & concurrency survey for Helix.ai Dedicated
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@helix.ai>, Priya Nair <priya@helix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-05T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pre-sales: peak curve & concurrency survey for Helix.ai Dedicated

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. To size a Dedicated fleet that matches Helix.ai's SLAs and cost targets we need a short, concrete workload profile from you. I've attached a small CSV template — if you can fill the sample rows (or paste a small export) we can convert this directly into a capacity sketch.

Primary questions we need answered:
- Typical and peak requests per second (RPS) by 15-min window (last 30 days if available)
- Prompt length distribution (tokens): median, 95th, max
- Response length distribution (tokens): median, 95th, max
- Concurrent sessions or long-lived chat sessions (avg duration, backpressure behaviour)
- % of sessions that use streaming vs non-streaming
- Session stickiness (do users usually hit the same model/session state?)
- Any heavy tool-calls or multimodal attachments that increase compute per request
- Target P99 latency and SLO tolerances for degradation vs cost tradeoffs

Two things I noticed on the quick notes from the call: you expect sustained daytime concurrency with 10x short bursts during product launches, and many chats include long 2–3k token prompts (few). If accurate, that pushes us toward reserved GPUs with burst capacity and KV caching enabled.

Please attach the CSV (helix_workload_sample.csv) and any existing telemetry exports. If it's easier, we can run a 30-min live sizing session next week — link at the end.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai
Book sizing call: https://cal.redwood.ai/soojin/30
From: Alex Rivera <alex@helix.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@helix.ai>
Date: 2027-10-05T17:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-sales: peak curve & concurrency survey for Helix.ai Dedicated

Hi Soojin,

Thanks — attaching the CSV export (helix_workload_sample.csv) and our draft SLA (SLA_draft_v2.pdf). I pasted quick answers inline below and included the CSV with 14 days of 1-min telemetry aggregated to 15-min buckets.

Inline summary:
- Typical daytime RPS: 45–60 RPS (15-min avg)
- Peak short bursts: up to 520 RPS for ~3–7 minutes during launches
- Prompt length (tokens): median 120, p95 780, max 3120 (rare ~0.2% of requests)
- Response length: median 90, p95 640, max 2100
- Concurrent sessions: steady-state 600 concurrent sessions, spikes to 4,200 concurrent sessions during launches (sessions last 2–10 minutes; median 3.5m)
- Streaming usage: ~35% of sessions use streaming (mostly customer-facing chat)
- Session stickiness: high — many sessions reuse a session state for the duration of the conversation (KV cache valuable)
- Tool-calls: ~5% of requests invoke heavy external tools (embeddings + search), which increase CPU/IO cost more than GPU time
- Target: P99 generation latency <= 650ms for interactive paths; for batch/analytics paths we can tolerate up to 2s

Notes:
- The max-token requests are rare but business-critical; we prefer graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or queued background generation) over dropping requests.
- We already run quantized models in prod for some workloads.

Let me know if the CSV format works or if you need more detail. Happy to have the sizing call Wed/Thu next week.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform, Helix.ai
alex@helix.ai
Attachments: helix_workload_sample.csv, SLA_draft_v2.pdf

Subject: Fwd: Pre-sales: peak curve & concurrency survey for Helix.ai Dedicated

Marissa / Karthik,

Forwarding Helix's workload export and quick answers. Two items to flag before we sketch a Dedicated commitment:

1) Burst shape and tail risk
- They have regular daytime baseline (~50 RPS) and very short high peaks (~520 RPS for ~5 minutes). That pattern means autoscaling alone will either be expensive or slow; recommend reserved baseline + burst pool.

2) Long prompts + streaming mix
- Prompt max of ~3.1k tokens (rare) and streaming for ~35% of sessions. We should size KV-cache memory for session stickiness and enable streaming-friendly serving paths.

Suggested first pass for an estimate (very rough):
- Reserved baseline: 4x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (aim for predictable 50–100 RPS sustained with reasonable oversubscription)
- Burst pool: additional 2–4 GPUs on demand (or a higher-priority preemptible pool) to absorb short 500 RPS spikes for 5–10m windows.
- Config: enable KV cache, session affinity, and prefer 4-bit quantized model variant for general traffic; keep unquantized for the rare long-token generation paths or fallback policy.

Marissa: can you turn this into a short capacity sketch with cost delta (reserved vs burst) and a canary rollout plan? Include a conservative SLA fallback that uses a smaller model or queued batch for long-token requests.

Karthik: please look at oversubscription ratios for A100-80GB with the reported 95th token sizes and streaming overhead; note that tool-calls increase CPU/IO more than GPU compute.

Alex / Priya: would you prefer we include a few scenario rows in the estimate (conservative, expected, aggressive)? Also share any constraints on regions/hardware preference — Helix prefers us-west for latency.

Thanks — I penciled in a 30-min sizing workshop on Wed 10/13 10:00 PDT if that works. Link: https://cal.redwood.ai/soojin/30

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai
